Answer: F
Reason: The axial CT image (Figure 2) demonstrates an ill-defined parenchymal consolidation in the posterior aspect of the left lower lobe, corresponding to the apical (superior) segment, with visible narrowing of the feeding bronchus and no associated mediastinal lymphadenopathy. This radiographic pattern of peripheral, non-segmental consolidation with airway involvement but without nodal enlargement is characteristic of bronchiolitis obliterans organizing pneumonia (BOOP).
